records.plant_name: Kirène Cement second power plant (Les Ciments du Sahel)
records.monitor_reason: Status unknown: the 54 MW plant (6×MAN 9L51/60, explicitly 'a second power plant' distinct from the 2009 4×18V32/40 35 MW plant already in GEM as Kyrene Cement) was ordered/under construction per MAN's 2021-05-20 release ('en construction' per Agence Ecofin's mirror), but a targeted 2026 hunt found NO commissioning, completion, or operating evidence anywhere since — and the capacity/existence evidence is single-origin (MAN release; powermag/power-eng are mirrors of it).
records.researcher_notes: Rolls forward (enriched) from the update batch's monitor lane. MAN's own PDF is now verified live (man-es.com press-release PDF; the HTML page is dead). africa-energy.com has a database record 'ciments-du-sahel-kirene-hfo-lfo' whose Status/capacity/commissioning fields are paywalled — worth checking if GEM has subscription access; visible fuel field says 'HFO, Other fuel oils'. Cement-line context: the expansion line the plant serves was commissioned Feb 2023 (Global Cement), so the power plant plausibly operates by now — but that is inference, not evidence. 54 MW clears the threshold, so this promotes to newplants the moment one independent status source appears.
records.action: Monitor — recheck by 2026-11 (try africa-energy DB via subscription, Senelec annual report IPP/autoproducteur tables, and fresh French-press sweep).

records.monitor_reason: Below the 50 MW threshold: ~23 MW captive plant (Wärtsilä 32 engines + gensets) at the Boto gold mine (Boto SA / Managem group), operating ~Q1 2025 per Wärtsilä's own releases.
records.researcher_notes: Well-evidenced (two Wärtsilä primary releases, 2024-09-27 and 2025-09-19) but permanently under threshold unless the mine expands generation ≥50 MW. Recheck is a low-priority existence check for expansion only.
records.action: Monitor — recheck by 2027-08 for capacity expansion only.

records.plant_name: Grande Côte Opérations Diogo power plant (Eramet)
records.monitor_reason: Below the 50 MW threshold: 36 MW captive dual-fuel plant (4×Wärtsilä 20V34DF + 1×9L34DF, 2013) powering the GCO mineral-sands dredge operation at Diogo (Eramet).
records.researcher_notes: Wärtsilä reference page + Eramet's own news page (hybridization with solar) — solid evidence, permanently under threshold. Eramet URL verified with accented token 'Grande Côte' (unaccented 'Grande Cote' fails).
records.action: Monitor — recheck by 2027-08 for capacity expansion only.

records.plant_name: ICS Mboro power plant (Industries Chimiques du Sénégal / Indorama)
records.monitor_reason: Below the 50 MW threshold (20 MW) AND fuel type unconfirmed: a targeted sweep of all accessible 2016 French press (Jeune Afrique, Setal, Sud Quotidien/allafrica, dakarmidi, lejecos, EnQuête+) found consistent facts — 20 MW, ~22bn CFA, Indorama-financed, in service Jun 2016, inaugurated 2016-12-16, surplus sold to Senelec — but NOT ONE names the fuel or technology, so GOGPT scope (gas/oil vs coal) cannot even be established.
records.researcher_notes: Permanently under threshold regardless of fuel; recorded so future Senegal batches don't re-research it from scratch. Pre-dates the 2020 retrospective window for status tracking anyway.
records.action: Monitor — low priority; drop candidate unless threshold policy changes.

records.monitor_reason: No specific site: FONSIS (Senegal's sovereign wealth fund) launched a tender/process for a 500 MW gas-fired IPP in Feb 2026, but no location, sponsor consortium, or concrete development step beyond the announcement — fails the named-site leg of the add threshold.
records.researcher_notes: agenceecofin also covered the FONSIS-led 500 MW tender (2026-02-16) but that page 403s to automated fetches — single verified source for now. Distinct from the Senelec Cap des Biches EPCF tender (see newplants) and from the Sandiara project. At 500 MW this is a major newplants candidate as soon as a site and awardee exist.
records.action: Monitor — recheck by 2026-12 (tender outcome, site selection).
